project.name: StudyLoop — fictional workshop demo
project.description: FICTIONAL TEACHING DEMO. A campus study-group idea used to practice evidence, uncertainty and decisions. All people, interviews and drafts are authored examples, not real research or adoption.
project.audience: Proposed: existing student study groups with unreliable attendance; not all students.
project.problem: Assumption to test: attendance uncertainty matters more than discovering more study partners.
questions: Tell me about the last time your study group met.
How did you decide who would attend?
What did you try to make coordination easier?
What worked well enough that you kept using it?
Who else has a different experience I should understand?
survey: After trying the proposed confirmation step, what happened?
What did you still have to do elsewhere?
What would you keep or change, and why?

changes.title: Narrow the audience
changes.body: Investigate existing groups with unreliable attendance; keep Nora as counterevidence.

changes.title: Test before building discovery
changes.body: Propose a simple confirmation flow; this is not yet a completed test.

changes.title: Compare with the current workaround
changes.body: Ask what the group already uses and what switching would cost.

experiments.hypothesis: PROPOSED FICTIONAL CASE: some existing groups will find attendance confirmation useful.
experiments.change: Invite up to five consenting groups to a one-week confirmation test and compare their own attendance records. Access, consent and baseline remain to be established.

outreach.title: Example route: a student club organizer
outreach.body: FICTIONAL DRAFT. Investigate whether an organizer hosts study sessions. Ask about access, rules and an appropriate way to invite voluntary participation. No permission is assumed.

outreach.title: Example invitation to review
outreach.body: FICTIONAL DRAFT. We are exploring whether a simple attendance confirmation helps existing study groups. If coordinating attendance is a problem you have experienced, could you show us your current routine? This is an early prototype; participation is optional.

outreach.title: Alternative route: an existing class community
outreach.body: FICTIONAL DRAFT. Identify one relevant community and ask its moderator about research posts. Do not claim a venue, policy or access is verified. No automated posting.
